title: Assistant bandleader: warming up the brass, and band personnel
summary: Caldwell opened shows with head numbers to warm up the brass, and lists a big band with George Mathews and Mack Madison.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: That's what they wanted at that particular time because he was neck and neck with Cab at that time, see. And we played a lot of big theaters behind Cab, and he went over just as big. So he'd called in me, asked me to be assistant band leader. Well, he didn't know that much about instrumentation, so like he would want the band -- hit the brass, hit them F's and G's, you know,

I said, Tiny, you don't call no numbers like that. The brass is too cold. Said, well, Hap, said, @Hight You're the assistant band leader, pay you (unintelligible) another little salary, so when we'd go on a job, we had the four Mills Brothers, we had a show like, you know, and so I said to the band, tune up. Don't read no music. Close the books. All head numbers. That'd give the brass time to warm their lips up. Say, all head numbers, don't turn no books, nothing but F's and G's in there for the brass.

So we had three trombones. We had three trumpets. Now, he wasn't going to call numbers with none of them F's and G's, and time to come out and play the number for (unintelligible), the guys have no lips.
We had George -- we had George Mathews.
Oh, he was a good man.
Very good man, an arranger too.

And we had a fellow named Green on trombone. I don't know what ever happened to that guy. Very good trombone player. And we had Max Maddox Mack Madison on trumpet. We had -- that's a boy -- he committed suicide. I don't know what ever happened to him -- after he came back from the war.
Well, I mean it was a full size, big * Lincoln Mills
Oh, big size, yes, four reeds, five brass, four rhythms.
Oh. Well, how long did you go with that?
